question.text: Which lane should you normally drive in, and when may you leave it?

answer.text: Drive in the right-hand lane unless you are passing, or stopped vehicles, a crash or another obstacle forces you over the center line, in which case yield to oncoming traffic first.

teaching.text: An obstacle lets you cross the center line, but oncoming drivers still go first. Remember: keep right unless passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drive in the right-hand lane unless you are passing, or stopped vehicles, a crash or another obstacle forces you over the center line, in which case yield to oncoming traffic first.

question.text: On which roads and with which signs may you also leave the right lane?

answer.text: Leaving the right lane is also allowed on roads with three or more marked lanes, on one-way streets with two or more lanes, and when signs or signals on a two-way multi-lane highway direct you left.

teaching.text: Wide roads, multi-lane one-way streets and directing signs all allow leaving the right lane. Remember: many lanes, one-way, signs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Leaving the right lane is also allowed on roads with three or more marked lanes, on one-way streets with two or more lanes, and when signs or signals on a two-way multi-lane highway direct you left.

question.text: When may you cross the center line to turn?

answer.text: You may cross the center line to turn left into or out of an alley, private road or driveway.

teaching.text: Reaching an alley, private road or driveway on the far side is a reason to cross the center line. Remember: alleys and driveways allow crossing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may cross the center line to turn left into or out of an alley, private road or driveway.

question.text: When may you leave the right lane for emergencies or construction?

answer.text: You may leave the right lane to go around a stopped emergency vehicle once it is safe, or when road construction is near or blocking the right lane or shoulder.

teaching.text: Give stopped responders and road crews room, but only once it is safe. Remember: around responders and roadwork.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may leave the right lane to go around a stopped emergency vehicle once it is safe, or when road construction is near or blocking the right lane or shoulder.

question.text: Where must slow vehicles stay?

answer.text: Slow vehicles must stay in the right lane except to pass or turn left.

teaching.text: Slow traffic keeps right so faster drivers can pass without weaving. Remember: slow traffic keeps right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Slow vehicles must stay in the right lane except to pass or turn left.

question.text: Who may drive against the flow of traffic?

answer.text: Only emergency and police vehicles running lights and sirens may drive against the flow of traffic.

teaching.text: No ordinary driver may go against traffic; only emergency and police vehicles with lights and sirens may. Remember: only lights and sirens.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Only emergency and police vehicles running lights and sirens may drive against the flow of traffic.

question.text: On a freeway, when may you use the left lane?

answer.text: On an interstate or full-access controlled freeway you must keep right, using the left lane only when congestion or weather requires it or an obstacle or hazard sits in the right lane.

teaching.text: Freeway left-lane use needs a listed reason, such as congestion, weather or a right-lane hazard. Remember: freeway: keep right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On an interstate or full-access controlled freeway you must keep right, using the left lane only when congestion or weather requires it or an obstacle or hazard sits in the right lane.

question.text: What other reasons allow the freeway left lane?

answer.text: On those freeways you may also use the left lane to move over for emergency or construction vehicles, or when no traffic is right behind or ahead of you in that lane.

teaching.text: Moving over for responders and crews, or an empty lane around you, also allow the freeway left lane. Remember: move over, or empty lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On those freeways you may also use the left lane to move over for emergency or construction vehicles, or when no traffic is right behind or ahead of you in that lane.

question.text: Is weaving between lanes to speed through traffic allowed?

answer.text: Weaving between lanes to speed through traffic is illegal.

teaching.text: Darting between lanes to get ahead is illegal on any road. Remember: no weaving, ever.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Weaving between lanes to speed through traffic is illegal.

question.text: May you drive across a median, and when may you use a cut-through?

answer.text: Driving across median strips or through barriers is illegal, but you may turn left through a paved median cut-through when no sign forbids it.

teaching.text: A grass median or a barrier is never a road, but a paved cut-through without a prohibiting sign is. Remember: cut-through yes, median no.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driving across median strips or through barriers is illegal, but you may turn left through a paved median cut-through when no sign forbids it.

question.text: Where may you enter and leave controlled-access roads?

answer.text: Enter and leave controlled-access roads only at designated, posted entrances and exits.

teaching.text: Controlled-access roads tell you where to get on and off; use only those posted points. Remember: posted entrances and exits only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Enter and leave controlled-access roads only at designated, posted entrances and exits.

question.text: How is a median cut-through different from crossing a median?

answer.text: A paved median cut-through with no prohibiting sign may be used for a left turn, while driving across median strips or through barriers is illegal.

teaching.text: The paved cut-through and the missing prohibiting sign are what make the turn legal. Remember: paved cut-through, sign permitting.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A paved median cut-through with no prohibiting sign may be used for a left turn, while driving across median strips or through barriers is illegal.

question.text: How is driving in an empty freeway left lane different from weaving?

answer.text: On a freeway, an empty left lane with no one right behind or ahead of you is a listed reason you may drive there, while weaving through traffic is never allowed.

teaching.text: Staying in an empty lane is allowed; jumping between lanes is not. Remember: empty lane fine, weaving never.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a freeway, an empty left lane with no one right behind or ahead of you is a listed reason you may drive there, while weaving through traffic is never allowed.

question.text: What steps make a safe right turn?

answer.text: For a right turn, use the correct lane and your signal, obey signs and signals, yield to pedestrians, emergency vehicles and other traffic, and check that your left side is clear.

teaching.text: Traffic from the left is what you pull in front of on a right turn, so check that side last. Remember: lane, signal, yield, check left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a right turn, use the correct lane and your signal, obey signs and signals, yield to pedestrians, emergency vehicles and other traffic, and check that your left side is clear.

question.text: How do you steer through a right turn?

answer.text: During a right turn, follow the curve of the curb and stay out of other lanes.

teaching.text: A tight right turn along the curb keeps you out of other lanes. Remember: hug the curb.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: During a right turn, follow the curve of the curb and stay out of other lanes.

question.text: What do trucks and buses need when turning right?

answer.text: Trucks and buses need extra room to turn right.

teaching.text: Never squeeze between a turning truck or bus and the curb. Remember: big vehicles swing wide.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Trucks and buses need extra room to turn right.

question.text: With multiple right-turn lanes, where do you finish the turn?

answer.text: With multiple right-turn lanes, finish the turn in the lane that matches the one you turned from, since drifting can cut off another driver and cause a crash.

teaching.text: Inner lane to inner lane, outer lane to outer lane, on a double right turn. Remember: stay in your lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: With multiple right-turn lanes, finish the turn in the lane that matches the one you turned from, since drifting can cut off another driver and cause a crash.

question.text: What steps make a safe left turn?

answer.text: For a left turn, use the correct lane and signal, obey signs and signals, and yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, emergency vehicles and other traffic.

teaching.text: On a left turn you yield to everyone crossing your path, including pedestrians and bicyclists. Remember: lane, signal, yield to all.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a left turn, use the correct lane and signal, obey signs and signals, and yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, emergency vehicles and other traffic.

question.text: How should your front wheels point before a left turn begins?

answer.text: Keep your front wheels pointed straight until you actually begin a left turn.

teaching.text: Straight wheels mean a push from behind sends you forward, not into oncoming traffic. Remember: wheels straight until turning.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Keep your front wheels pointed straight until you actually begin a left turn.

question.text: With multiple left-turn lanes, where do you end the turn?

answer.text: With multiple left-turn lanes, end the turn in the lane that corresponds to your turn lane.

teaching.text: On a double left turn, your turn lane decides your finishing lane. Remember: match your turn lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: With multiple left-turn lanes, end the turn in the lane that corresponds to your turn lane.

question.text: What should you look for before turning left?

answer.text: Check all approaching traffic before a left turn, looking for vehicles hidden behind or beside others, especially motorcycles, scooters and bicycles, which are easy to miss.

teaching.text: Look past and beside the first vehicle, because small road users hide behind big ones. Remember: find the hidden motorcycle.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Check all approaching traffic before a left turn, looking for vehicles hidden behind or beside others, especially motorcycles, scooters and bicycles, which are easy to miss.

question.text: Why stay in your matching lane in a double turn lane?

answer.text: In a double turn lane, staying in your matching lane prevents cutting off the driver turning beside you.

teaching.text: The driver beside you is turning too, so drifting puts you in their path. Remember: drifting cuts off neighbors.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a double turn lane, staying in your matching lane prevents cutting off the driver turning beside you.

question.text: What do you do with your wheels while waiting to turn left?

answer.text: While waiting to turn left, hold the front wheels straight ahead and turn them only as the turn begins.

teaching.text: Wait with wheels straight, and turn them only when you start moving. Remember: straight while waiting.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: While waiting to turn left, hold the front wheels straight ahead and turn them only as the turn begins.

question.text: Must you signal turns, and who mostly uses hand signals now?

answer.text: Always signal turns; hand signals for left, right and stop are now used mostly by motorcyclists, scooter and moped riders and bicyclists.

teaching.text: Signal every turn, and read a rider's raised or extended arm as a signal. Remember: always signal.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Always signal turns; hand signals for left, right and stop are now used mostly by motorcyclists, scooter and moped riders and bicyclists.

question.text: How do you move one lane to the left?

answer.text: To move left, check behind and to your left with a head check, signal left, and move over carefully.

teaching.text: Your blind spot on the left is covered by the head check before you signal. Remember: look left, signal, move.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To move left, check behind and to your left with a head check, signal left, and move over carefully.

question.text: How do you move one lane to the right?

answer.text: To move right, check behind and to your right, signal right, and move over carefully.

teaching.text: Before moving right, turn your head to cover the right-side blind spot. Remember: look right, signal, move.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To move right, check behind and to your right, signal right, and move over carefully.

question.text: How do the head checks differ for moving left and moving right?

answer.text: A lane change to the left starts with a head check behind and to your left, while a change to the right checks behind and to your right.

teaching.text: The side you move toward is the side you check. Remember: check the side you move.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A lane change to the left starts with a head check behind and to your left, while a change to the right checks behind and to your right.

question.text: What is a roundabout, and whom do entering drivers yield to?

answer.text: A roundabout is a circular intersection where traffic moves counterclockwise around a central island and entering vehicles yield to traffic coming from the left, including bicyclists and pedestrians.

teaching.text: Traffic in the circle comes from your left, so that is where you yield. Remember: counterclockwise, yield left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A roundabout is a circular intersection where traffic moves counterclockwise around a central island and entering vehicles yield to traffic coming from the left, including bicyclists and pedestrians.

question.text: How should you approach a roundabout?

answer.text: When approaching a roundabout, use signs and pavement markings to pick the right lane, slow down, stay right of the center island, and look left as you reach the yield line.

teaching.text: Pick your lane early, slow down, and look left as you reach the yield line. Remember: pick lane, slow, look left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When approaching a roundabout, use signs and pavement markings to pick the right lane, slow down, stay right of the center island, and look left as you reach the yield line.

question.text: How do you enter a roundabout, and what must you never do?

answer.text: Enter a roundabout when a suitable gap appears and merge with the flow, and never turn left to enter, which puts you in front of oncoming traffic.

teaching.text: Join the circle with a gentle merge; turning left to enter meets traffic head on. Remember: merge on a gap.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Enter a roundabout when a suitable gap appears and merge with the flow, and never turn left to enter, which puts you in front of oncoming traffic.

question.text: Whom should you watch for as you enter or exit a roundabout?

answer.text: Watch for pedestrians crossing as you enter or exit a roundabout.

teaching.text: Crosswalks sit at roundabout entries and exits, right where you join and leave. Remember: walkers at every crossing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Watch for pedestrians crossing as you enter or exit a roundabout.

question.text: Who has the right of way inside a roundabout, and when may you stop?

answer.text: While traveling inside a roundabout, keep right of the center island; vehicles in the roundabout hold the right of way, and you must not stop unless stopping is the only safe way to avoid a collision or other danger.

teaching.text: Once circulating you have the right of way, and you stop only to avoid a crash. Remember: stop only for collision or danger.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: While traveling inside a roundabout, keep right of the center island; vehicles in the roundabout hold the right of way, and you must not stop unless stopping is the only safe way to avoid a collision or other danger.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: stop only for collision or danger

question.text: How do you leave a roundabout?

answer.text: You leave a roundabout by turning right onto the road you want.

teaching.text: Every roundabout exit is a right turn onto your road. Remember: exit with a right turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You leave a roundabout by turning right onto the road you want.

question.text: An emergency vehicle approaches while you are in a roundabout. What do you do?

answer.text: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are in a roundabout, do not stop; leave at the nearest exit, pull right and stop to let it pass.

teaching.text: A siren in the circle means leave at the next exit, then pull right and stop. Remember: exit first, then stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are in a roundabout, do not stop; leave at the nearest exit, pull right and stop to let it pass.

question.text: When should you choose your roundabout lane?

answer.text: Choose your lane before entering a roundabout and avoid changing lanes inside it.

teaching.text: Lane changes inside a curving circle are hard to judge, so pick your lane first. Remember: choose before you enter.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Choose your lane before entering a roundabout and avoid changing lanes inside it.

question.text: How should you treat trucks and other vehicles in a roundabout?

answer.text: Avoid passing or driving beside trucks and trailers in a roundabout, as they may need more than one lane, and do not pass other vehicles, bicycles or mopeds.

teaching.text: Trucks may use more than one lane in a roundabout, so never ride beside or pass them. Remember: never pass in the circle.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Avoid passing or driving beside trucks and trailers in a roundabout, as they may need more than one lane, and do not pass other vehicles, bicycles or mopeds.

question.text: How do you exit a roundabout, and what if you miss your exit?

answer.text: When exiting, keep a slow speed, signal your exit, and wait to accelerate until you are past the exit's pedestrian crossing; if you miss your exit, go around again.

teaching.text: Exit slowly with a signal, speed up only past the crosswalk, and circle again if you miss it. Remember: missed it? go around.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When exiting, keep a slow speed, signal your exit, and wait to accelerate until you are past the exit's pedestrian crossing; if you miss your exit, go around again.

question.text: Whom do you yield to entering a roundabout, and who yields to you inside?

answer.text: Entering a roundabout you yield to traffic from your left, but once inside you have the right of way over drivers waiting to enter.

teaching.text: Yield to the left when entering; inside, waiting drivers yield to you. Remember: yield entering, go inside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Entering a roundabout you yield to traffic from your left, but once inside you have the right of way over drivers waiting to enter.

question.text: Do you stop in a roundabout for an emergency vehicle?

answer.text: In a roundabout you do not stop for an approaching emergency vehicle; you leave by the nearest exit and only then pull right and stop.

teaching.text: Stopping in the circle traps you and the emergency vehicle, so exit first. Remember: never stop in the circle.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a roundabout you do not stop for an approaching emergency vehicle; you leave by the nearest exit and only then pull right and stop.

question.text: How do you enter and exit a roundabout?

answer.text: You enter a roundabout by merging with the counterclockwise flow and exit by turning right, never by turning left.

teaching.text: You never turn left at either end of a roundabout. Remember: merge in, turn right out.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You enter a roundabout by merging with the counterclockwise flow and exit by turning right, never by turning left.

question.text: How do you fix a missed roundabout exit?

answer.text: Missing your roundabout exit is fixed by circling around again, not by stopping or changing lanes inside the circle.

teaching.text: Going around again costs a little time and avoids risky stops and lane changes. Remember: circle again, no stopping.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Missing your roundabout exit is fixed by circling around again, not by stopping or changing lanes inside the circle.

question.text: What should you do at every railroad crossing, and why?

answer.text: Slow down and look both ways at every railroad crossing, because a train can need a mile or more to stop and is closer and faster than it looks.

teaching.text: A train cannot stop or swerve for you, so slow down and look every time. Remember: trains are closer than they look.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Slow down and look both ways at every railroad crossing, because a train can need a mile or more to stop and is closer and faster than it looks.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: trains are closer than they look

question.text: Where may people cross tracks, and what is illegal on them?

answer.text: Walkers, cyclists and drivers should cross tracks only at designated crossings, and walking along or stopping on tracks is illegal.

teaching.text: Designated crossings are the only safe places to cross tracks. Remember: cross only at crossings.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Walkers, cyclists and drivers should cross tracks only at designated crossings, and walking along or stopping on tracks is illegal.

question.text: What does the railroad advance warning sign mean, and where do you stop for a train?

answer.text: The railroad advance warning sign means a crossing is ahead; with a train coming, stop no more than fifty feet and no less than fifteen feet from the tracks.

teaching.text: With a train coming, choose a stopping spot between fifty and fifteen feet from the tracks. Remember: fifty to fifteen feet.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The railroad advance warning sign means a crossing is ahead; with a train coming, stop no more than fifty feet and no less than fifteen feet from the tracks.

question.text: How far do trains overhang the rails?

answer.text: Trains overhang the rails by at least three feet on each side, and cargo can stick out farther.

teaching.text: Being off the rails is not enough, because the train is wider than the track. Remember: trains are wider than tracks.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Trains overhang the rails by at least three feet on each side, and cargo can stick out farther.

question.text: Where must you stop when a train approaches, and how far do trains overhang the tracks?

answer.text: When a train approaches a railroad crossing, all vehicles must stop between fifteen and fifty feet from the tracks, and trains overhang the rails by at least three feet on each side with cargo possibly extending farther.

teaching.text: The fifteen-foot near limit leaves room for the overhang and any cargo sticking out. Remember: fifteen to fifty feet; three-foot overhang.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a train approaches a railroad crossing, all vehicles must stop between fifteen and fifty feet from the tracks, and trains overhang the rails by at least three feet on each side with cargo possibly extending farther.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: fifteen to fifty feet; three-foot overhang
